content.comment_body: Hello, I'm searching for a basic 0-1 switch to adjust input values so that the [product_name] functions as needed (for controlling hours of light per day). I can handle the programming part: with an input of "0", lights stay on for 22 hours, with "1", the cycle changes to 6 hours. However, I'm unsure what type of switch fits these input requirements: signal 0 - < 5V DC, < 0.85mA; signal 1 - > 8.5V DC, > 1.5mA. I haven't found a suitable option yet. Could someone please recommend a cheap switch available in the UK, and share wiring advice? Thank you!

Hello [user_name], you can use any switch or relay with a normally closed (NC) contact. The wiring diagram in the [product_name] documentation should guide you. For reference, some relevant switches are available as follows: [company_name] BETA: [article_no]; [company_name] DELTA: [article_no]. You can also implement the 22hr/6hr control via selector settings (e.g., C1-C4) on the [product_name]. More information is available in the instructions: [url]
Yes, you can use a standard switch like the ones commonly used for house lights. Any typical switch should work.

Thanks for the advice, both responses clarified things for me. So if I use a regular household switch, when it's OFF, the supply (12V) won't connect — giving 0V, which meets the <5V input for "0" on the [product_name]. When ON, 12V (>8.5V) flows — this sets the input as "1". Is my understanding correct?

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centers around selecting and connecting a simple switch to control input states for a [product_name] device, with the goal of toggling light cycles. Users value clear hardware guidance, practical wiring help, and confirmation that general household switches are suitable for this application. The confusion mainly arises about matching electrical signal levels to input requirements.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to buy an inexpensive, standard switch that works with the [product_name] input, and receive clear wiring instructions for easy setup and integration with common household hardware.
